Rules changed since the standard (2026-10-22-c at 3e3581d), per git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/: testing.md renamed ex_unit.md with a wider trigger row; the Formatting bullet under "How to use this skill" is new; Before you finish step 1 now reads "Run `mix format path/to/file.ex` on any changed file you have not formatted since its last edit (see "Formatting" under "How to use this skill")"; "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body..." were reworded; Assert with patterns' == sentence was reworded with a new example. Of the case's seven rules only Before you finish changed, and its step 1 sentence decides that step: a changed file left unformatted after its last edit breaks it. The Formatting bullet itself is not a graded heading; its timing is graded as the case's check line, as check-10 did. The other six rules are graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard (a literal map or list of the accepted code strings counts as clean under the atoms rule; a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so; a one-step with is a violation, a case for a single fallible call is not exercised).

The check line "`mix format path` runs on each file before the session edits another file or runs the tests..." is met in 0 of 4 runs. Order of Write, Edit and mix format calls (#n is the tool-call number). haiku-1: Write lib/shop/cart.ex (#6); Edit test/shop/cart_test.exs x5 (#8-#12); a refused chain (#13) that would have run `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null; mix compile...; mix test...; mix credo --strict`; then `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix compile --warnings-as-errors 2>&1 | tail -20` (#14); `mix test` (#15); `mix credo --strict; sed -n 60,70p lib/shop/cart.ex` (#16); Edit lib/shop/cart.ex (#17, one @doc sentence); `mix format --check-formatted lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && echo FORMAT_OK && mix test && mix credo --strict` (#18). cart.ex was left for five test edits before its first format; after the session came back to it at #17 it ran only a format check, not `mix format`, before the final tests. haiku-2: Write cart.ex (#4); Edit cart_test.exs x2 (#6, #7); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs 2>&1 | tail -5; git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null; mix test 2>&1 | tail -40` (#8); Edit cart_test.exs (#9, adds doctest); a refused chain (#10); `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` (#11); `mix format --check-formatted lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && echo FORMAT_OK` (#12); `mix test && mix credo --strict` (#13). cart.ex was left for two test edits before its format, and the test file was edited again at #9 and only checked before the final tests. sonnet-1: a refused python3 heredoc (#3) that would have rewritten both files and then run `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex && mix format test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix compile --force; mix test`; Write cart.ex (#4); Write cart_test.exs (#5); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex && mix format test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix compile --force 2>&1 | tail -5; mix test 2>&1 | tail -8` (#6). It formatted each file with its own command, but cart.ex was left for the test file before being formatted, and both formats came in the command that ran the tests. sonnet-2: a refused python3 heredoc (#7) of the same shape; Write cart.ex (#8); Edit cart_test.exs x2 (#9, #10); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex` (#11); Edit cart.ex x2 (#12, #13); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex && mix format test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix test 2>&1 | tail -20` (#14); `mix credo --strict` (#15). cart.ex was left for two test edits before its first format at #11; it was formatted again after the session came back to it, but in the same command as the tests; the test file, edited at #9-#10, was formatted only at #14 after cart.ex had been edited in between. This is the closest of the four.

What the formatter changed, by replaying every Write and Edit onto the case's files and running `mix format` at each format call in the replay (the replayed files are byte-identical to each run's final files). haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1: no change in any run of the formatter. sonnet-2: `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex` (#11) changed one line, wrapping `    subtotal = Enum.sum_by(cart.items, fn {sku, quantity} -> Map.fetch!(prices, sku) * quantity end)` into `    subtotal =` / `      Enum.sum_by(...)`; its #14 run changed nothing. Whether the sessions read the formatter's output: `mix format` prints nothing, and no session ran a diff that could show a change (haiku-1's refused #13 and haiku-2's #8 chained `git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null`, which compares nothing). haiku-1's `sed -n 60,70p` at #16 looked at the apply_discount_code @doc, which it then edited, with no stated link to formatting. sonnet-2 did not read cart.ex after #11 either, but its next Edit (#12) gave the wrapped two-line form as its old_string, exactly as the formatter had left it, and replaced the line with `subtotal = subtotal(cart, prices)` plus a new `defp subtotal/2` (#13), then formatted again: it predicted the break and rewrote the broken line into a named helper, which is the response the Formatting bullet asks for. Its summary says "A separate `subtotal/2` helper keeps `total/2` short." Thinking blocks are redacted in all four transcripts, so no session's reasoning about formatting is visible.
